messages.author: 238422c6037ad1c9
messages.subject: [Spatial Model] Error
parts:
Hello all, 
I am trying to build a Leroux model for spatial correlation following the Bugs code of MacNab et al (2006), the code is in the appendix A of the related paper, at the moment of building the model using the function "nimbleModel(code, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)" I am getting the following error:

defining model...
Error in permute.vertices(graph, oldGraphID_2_newGraphID) : 
  At topology.c:2725 : Permute vertices: invalid permutation vector size, Invalid value
In addition: Warning message:
In topological.sort(graph, mode = "out") :
  At structural_properties.c:3346 :graph contains a cycle, partial result is returned

Any idea of what is happening here? and how to fix it? 
Thank you in advance!
MacNab, Y. C., Kmetic, A., Gustafson, P., & Sheps, S. (2006). An innovative application of Bayesian disease mapping methods to patient safety research: A Canadian adverse medical event study. Statistics in medicine, 25(23), 3960-3980.

Dear Daniel and all, 
Thank you for your quick response, below is the code of nimble that I am using. 
Let me know if you need more information about it, Thank you in advance 

code <- nimbleCode({
  # likelihood
  for(k in 1:Num.Areas){
    O[k]~dpois(b[k]) # count follow a poisson distribution
    log(b[k])<-log(E[k])+mu+phi[k] 
     #E for the expected values, mu average mean, phi random effect that model the spatial correlation
  }
  
   for(k in 1:length(nbInfo$num)){ # length(nbInfo$num) total number of neighbors 
    phi.off[k]<-phi[adj[k]]
   }
  
  #now the distribution of the random part 
  #the off1[] and off2[] vectors creates a flag of where to start and end the sum of the neighbor areas
  #Num[] is the number of neighbors of area K 
  for(k in 1:Num.Areas) {
    phi.mu[k]<-(rho*sum( phi.off[(off1[k]+1):(off2[k])] ))  /((Num[k]*rho)+1-rho) 
    phi.std[k]<- tau^2/((Num[k]*rho)+1-rho)
    
    phi[k] ~ dnorm(mean=phi.mu[k], sd=phi.std[k])         
  }
  # priors
  mu~dnorm(0,0.0001)
  rho ~ dunif(0, 1)
  tau~dgamma(0.01,0.01)
})

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: [Spatial Model] Error
parts:
Hi Diego, to follow up on the general issue here.

1) Nimble (JAGS as well) does not allow for cycles. So to specify a CAR model in nimble you must specify the joint distribution for all the random effects as a vector (please see the manual chapter on CAR models). The specification in Nimble is similar to the dcar specifications in GeoBUGS.

2) I don't see in the GeoBUGS documentation that cycles are allowed, but given that MacNab et al. (2006) have such BUGS code with cycles and that the BUGS manual does not say cycles are not allowed, presumably it is possible. Here is a post on the JAGS mailing list in which this is discussed. Note that in the post, Martyn Plummer (the JAGS developer)  cautions the user that just because an MCMC runs in (Open)BUGS doesn't mean the MCMC is valid (in particular the issue he is concerned with is whether the conditional distributions specified give a coherent joint distribution). I would suspect that if the conditionals are correctly specified the MCMC output from BUGS would be valid.

Chris
